turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Sorry, the number 12 bus just sat there on third street, and then I walked in the wrong door by the pharmacy. Umm, the reason I came is my bones hurt, my legs mostly.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'm glad you got here. Sit, take a breath. What's been happening with the pain?

[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): Both thighs, deep, like inside the bone, not the muscle. It started two days ago, I was on the couch watching a game and it just showed up. I have sickle cell, so this is the kind of pain I know, but I still wanted someone to look.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. Two days, both thighs. How strong is it, and what makes it ease off or flare?

[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Sitting still it's about a 6 out of 10. If I walk, err, even to the bathroom, it climbs, and a warm shower last night helped for maybe an hour. Rest helps a little, but it's there the whole time, it doesn't come and go.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fever or chills mixed in with this?

[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): I feel warm, kind of flushed, not shaking chills. My little thermometer at home, the cheap white one from the drugstore, said about 100 this morning, and then just now it was 38.1 when it got checked out front. I always mix up fahrenheit and celsius, my sister's the one who thinks in metric because she lived in Toronto for a year, which is a whole other story.
[SEG0008] person_3 (NURSE): Mm. That 38.1 was me. Temperature 38.1, heart rate 96, blood pressure 122 over 74, oxygen sat 99 percent on room air, and he's sitting comfortably.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thanks. You said sickle cell. Tell me about that, and what medicines you take for it.

[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): They caught it on the newborn screen, so my whole life, I'm 24. I take folic acid, 1 milligram by mouth every morning, and hydroxurea, two 500 milligram capsules by mouth, so a thousand milligrams once a day. My older brother has sickle cell too, he coached me through the first bad pain I remember back in middle school, but that's old news.

[SEG0011] person_3 (NURSE): Before I forget, his mom caught me in the hallway. She said he does not take the tablets on Sundays, she said he sleeps badly, and that cut on his hand healed in five days.

[SEG0012] person_1 (PATIENT): No, uh, that's off. I skip the hydroxurea on Saturdays, not Sundays, the folic acid I take every single day. I do not sleep badly, I sleep fine, around seven hours, I just stay up on my phone some nights. The cut was a paper cut from a cardboard box at work and it healed in five days, normal, not slow or anything.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay, Saturdays, I'll go with what you're telling me. Any cuts or sores that have been slow to heal?

[SEG0014] person_1 (PATIENT): No. That paper cut closed in five days and I stopped covering it after the first day. I don't get slow healing sores, I check because people say sickle cell can do that, but mine don't.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain, or trouble catching your breath?

[SEG0016] person_1 (PATIENT): No chest pain, and no shortness of breath. I was specifically watching for that, the acute chest thing they warned me about last year, and it isn't happening. I can take a full breath, it just doesn't feel nice in my legs when I stand to do it.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): What about your stomach, any nausea? And does it hurt when you pee?

[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): No nausea. I've been eating a bit less, just because getting up to cook is a whole thing with the legs, but my stomach itself is fine. Peeing is normal, no burning, the color is my usual yellow.

[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): Oh, and my sister keeps pushing her biotin on me, the 5000 microgram hair vitamins, she takes two a day for her own hair. I don't take those. I told her I'm not starting somebody else's pills.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ha, yeah, we'll leave your sister's biotin alone. I'm more interested in how you're getting around at home.

[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): I live alone, second floor, no elevator, which is annoying this week. I work packing boxes at the warehouse on elm, on my feet most of the shift. I called out yesterday and today, and my manager was fine about it, surprisingly.

[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's a lot of stairs. Let me examine you. Both thighs are tender when I press, more on the left, no swelling, skin not red, lungs are clear and your heart sounds regular.

[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): Yeah the left is the boss of the two, I meant to say that earlier. When you press the middle it zings right down toward my knee. The right is there but quieter, more of a dull ache than a zing.

[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): That lines up. I think this is a mild vaso-occlusive episode, a pain crisis, with a low grade fever, on the background of your sickle cell. I'm not worried it's acute chest today, and I'm not locking it in as anything worse until we see the labs.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'd like blood tests today, a complete blood count, a reticulocyte count, and a basic chemistry to see where your hydration is.
[SEG0026] person_3 (NURSE): Right. I can draw all of that before you go. Lab's still open, shouldn't take long.

[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay. Last time they stuck me three times, my veins hide, especially if I'm a little dry, so the left forearm usually works better, just saying. And will the hydroxurea and the folic acid stay the same?

[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, keep the folic acid and the hydroxurea just like you take them, and be straight with me about those Saturdays. For the pain I'm starting ibuprofen 600 milligrams by mouth every 6 hours with food, only for the next few days. And push fluids, water, more than your usual, all day.

[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): Ibuprofen with food, got it. I have a sensitive stomach if I take pain stuff on empty, one time in college I took some leftover naproxen of my roommate's and I regretted it, so I won't do that again. How much water are we talking, like bottles, or just keep a glass going?
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): A glass every hour or so while you're awake is plenty, no need to force it. If your stomach burns on the ibuprofen, stop it and call us.

[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): Glass an hour, I can do that. I have that big blue bottle, it holds like 32 ounces, I'll just refill it. Should I stay off work? Those shifts are ten hours on concrete and I don't think my thighs are going to cooperate.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Stay off the warehouse floor until I see you again. I want you back in three days, we'll look at the labs and the pain together.

[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): Three days, okay. If the pain jumps or I get chest pain before that, I shouldn't wait, right? I just want to hear you say it so I don't talk myself out of the ER like I did one time back then, which was dumb, I know.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Please don't wait. If the pain gets a lot worse, or you get chest pain, trouble breathing, or the fever climbs, go to the ER. Otherwise I'll see you in three days.
[SEG0035] person_1 (PATIENT): ER for those things, clinic in three days. Umm, can I take the ibuprofen tonight even if I already had a little soup, does soup count as food?
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Soup counts. Take it with the soup, same 600 milligrams every 6 hours, and don't double up if you forget a dose.
[SEG0037] person_3 (NURSE): I'll grab the tubes and be right back. Left forearm, you said. You want water while you wait?
[SEG0038] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes please, water, and the left forearm, thank you. I ramble when I'm nervous, sorry, I know I gave you my whole life story including my sister's hair vitamins.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): You did fine. Rambling gives me the details. We'll get those labs, start the ibuprofen, fluids, and I'll see you in three days, and you can call sooner if you need to.
[SEG0040] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay. Thanks for not rushing me. I'll do the water, I'll skip work, and I'll actually take the hydroxurea, well, except I already told you about Saturdays.
[SEG0041] person_3 (NURSE): Of. Come on through when you're ready, the chair's open.

spec.situation: Young adult with known sickle cell disease and bone pains for two days, fever mild; takes folic acid and hydroxyurea; fluids and painkiller plan; blood tests planned.

traps.happens: A caregiver or relative reports observations ('the cut healed in five days', 'she sleeps badly', 'he does not take the tablets on Sundays'); the patient agrees, disagrees or corrects one point. The nurse also reports a measurement that the patient mentioned before.
traps.label_rule: reported_by follows who said it. A healing cut that healed normally is a negative finding (no slow-healing wounds) or nothing, NOT a symptom. A disputed fact is recorded with certainty disputed or as an uncertainty. A correction replaces the earlier value (Saturday, not Sunday).

features: third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.
doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).

bad.reason: Nurse relays mother said poor sleep, but patient directly denies sleeping badly.
bad.text: Poor sleep (category=neurological, status=present, temporality=current, reported_by=nurse, certainty=disputed)

bad.reason: Dose/route/current use supported, but frequency wrong: he skips Saturdays, so not simply once daily.
bad.text: hydroxyurea (dose=1000 mg, route=oral, frequency=once daily, indication=sickle cell disease, status=currently_used, reported_by=patient)

bad.reason: Folic acid every morning supported, but hydroxyurea 'once daily' is incomplete; patient skips Saturdays.
bad.text: Continue folic acid every morning and hydroxyurea once daily (action_type=counselling, status=recommended, responsible_person=patient)

bad.reason: No unresolved uncertainty; patient clarified Saturday skipping and doctor accepted it.
bad.text: Patient says he skips once-daily hydroxyurea on Saturdays, so it is not taken as prescribed. (type=adherence_uncertain, related_entities=medications[1], resolution_status=unresolved)

bad.reason: Conflict was resolved by patient denial; not unresolved.
bad.text: The nurse reports poor sleep, but the patient says he sleeps fine. (type=conflicting_statement, related_entities=symptoms[2], resolution_status=unresolved)

omissions.text: Hydroxyurea schedule was clarified: patient skips hydroxyurea on Saturdays, not Sundays; folic acid is taken every day. The recorded hydroxyurea frequency of 'once daily' is incomplete/wrong without the Saturday omission, and the Sunday report was rejected by the patient and accepted by the doctor.
The recorded symptom 'Poor sleep' is wrong: the patient explicitly denied sleeping badly and said he sleeps fine around seven hours, just sometimes stays up on his phone.
Pain details missing: pain is described as deep 'inside the bone, not the muscle.'
Pain laterality/detail missing: the left thigh is worse than the right by history; pressing the middle of the left thigh causes pain that 'zings' down toward the knee, while the right is a dull ache.
Additional negative urinary detail missing: urine color is his usual yellow.
Negative finding missing: no cuts or sores that have been slow to heal; paper cut healed normally in five days and was uncovered after the first day.
Doctor's assessment included that he is not worried about acute chest syndrome today.
Doctor also said he is not committing to anything worse until labs are back.
Instruction missing: do not double up ibuprofen doses if a dose is forgotten.
Follow-up instruction missing: patient may call sooner if needed.
